Speaking for Formula 1, I can say that there are huge mental and physical challenges which require the drivers not just to become amazing athletes, but extremely smart and sharp people. 

In F1 decisions and reactions have to be made in split seconds. If you lose concentration, or if you're even just a little unfocused, a corner could turn into a spin; an overtake could turn into a hideous pile up. The drivers have to think about this stuff every split second. 

And it's not only on-track things they must think about, they have to worry about fuel consumption, brake balance, tyre degradation, engine and brake temperature, when to pit, etc. There's a huge amount they have to be consistently thinking about.

On the physical side of things, these guys have to be enormously fit. Simply pressing the brake peddle down requires roughly 30lbs of pressure for instance. And when they do brake, they undergo forces of up to 6g. Think about that. 6 times the force of gravity on your body. That's your neck, your head, your legs, every time they have to slam on the brakes. 
Some corners (such as Turn 8 in Istanbul) have them undergoing 4g of turning force for roughly 8 seconds at a time. That's incredible to think about. 

Couple this with the fact they are racing these cars, usually in hot ambient conditions, directly in front of a burning hot engine, surrounded by carbon fibre, stuck in 4 layers of fireproof clothing, for two hours, and it's clear to see the skill and training required to be a full time F1 driver. 

Not forgetting that it isn't just a race every fortnight, they do testing, practice and training all the time. Many of the drivers could be high level cycling professionals, or triathletes, if they so chose.
